title: Tandroy dialect - Wikipedia
text: Tandroy (also called Antandroy or Ntandroy) is a dialect of the Malagasy language [2] spoken primarily by the Antandroy people in the Androy region of southern Madagascar. It is close to Mahafaly and Karimbola, the latter being considered a dialect of Tandroy.

title: Music of Madagascar - Wikipedia
text: Music in Madagascar tends toward major keys and diatonic scales, [6] although coastal music makes frequent use of minor keys, most likely due to early Arab influences at coastal ports of call. [7] Malagasy music has served a wide range of social, spiritual and mundane functions across the centuries.

title: Malagasy, Tandroy-Mahafaly Language (TDX) - Ethnologue
text: Tandroy-Mahafaly Malagasy is a stable indigenous language of Madagascar. It belongs to the Austronesian language family and is part of the Malagasy macrolanguage. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.
